meta.subtitle: Defense-driven growth and a net-cash balance sheet, tempered by GAAP losses and a rich multiple

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate nLIGHT a BUY with a target range of $46 to $68. The case rests on a defense-led revenue inflection: second-quarter 2026 revenue of $82.6 million rose {+ 33.8% +} year over year, and Aerospace and Defense now drives the bulk of the business. Gross margin and Adjusted EBITDA have turned up as volumes scale, while the balance sheet carries no debt after an equity raise. The offset is valuation and near-term execution risk: the shares trade at a rich multiple of sales and forward earnings, the company is still unprofitable on a GAAP basis, and third-quarter guidance was cut by supply-chain delays. Our probability-weighted fair value is $50.10, an expected upside of +21.6% against the $41.20 price, with bear-case downside of -27.2% and reward/risk of 0.79x. That reward-to-risk supports a BUY rather than a stronger rating.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: nLIGHT, Inc. designs, develops and manufactures high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, along with the components, modules and subsystems built around them. The company sells into three end markets, Aerospace and Defense, Industrial and Microfabrication, and runs the business as two reportable segments, Laser Products and Advanced Development. Its distinctive feature is vertical integration from the semiconductor chip through system-level products, which lets it reuse shared core technologies across applications from directed energy and laser sensing to additive manufacturing and semiconductor microfabrication. nLIGHT was incorporated in 2000, is headquartered in Camas, Washington, and employs more than 800 people across the United States, Europe and Asia. A defense-led ramp reshaped the top line in 2025 and delivered double-digit revenue growth after several years of decline.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: nLIGHT has become a defense-driven growth company that is not yet profitable on a GAAP basis. Revenue growth has reaccelerated year over year, led by directed energy and defense components, and the balance sheet is now net cash after an equity raise. Against that, the shares are expensive on sales and forward earnings, and the company still posts operating and net losses. Our call balances the two: a probability-weighted view supports a BUY with an expected upside of +21.6%, but a reward/risk of 0.79x, held back by valuation and near-term supply-chain disruption, keeps it short of a stronger rating.

catalysts: Directed energy is the swing factor: Aerospace and Defense revenue grew {+ 40.8% +} year over year in the second quarter of 2026, and management points to the Department of War's Joint Laser Weapon Systems award as a template for more program wins.
Recovery of the shipments delayed into later quarters is a near-term catalyst, since management expects to deliver them and has set third-quarter guidance below the second quarter's level.
Consensus sees revenue continuing to compound into 2027, and delivering against that path would support the multiple.
A net-cash balance sheet after the early-2026 equity raise lets nLIGHT fund research and capacity without adding debt.
risks: Profitability is the missing piece: nLIGHT is still loss-making on a GAAP basis, so its trailing earnings multiple is negative.
Valuation leaves little room for error, with the shares expensive on both sales and forward earnings.
Revenue is concentrated in defense and in a small number of customers, so budget cycles and program timing drive the outcome.
Supply-chain and export-control disruptions in China have already delayed shipments and could hit revenue and margins again.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue growth reaccelerated in 2025 and again in early 2026. Full-year 2025 revenue was $261.3 million, up {+ 31.6% +}, and growth carried into the second quarter of 2026. The more important change is the margin story. Gross margin rose to 29.8% in 2025 from 16.6% in 2024 on higher volumes and better cost absorption, and reached 31.1% in the second quarter of 2026 against 29.9% a year earlier. Operating margin remains negative, at -10.2% for 2025 and -4.4% in the second quarter, so the business is not yet profitable on a GAAP basis. GAAP net loss narrowed to $23.5 million in 2025 from $60.8 million in 2024, a $37.3 million improvement, while Adjusted EBITDA swung by $42.3 million to turn positive from a prior-year loss of $18.8 million. Diluted loss per share was $0.47 for 2025 and $0.02 in the second quarter.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet is a clear strength. nLIGHT strengthened its liquidity further in early 2026 through an equity raise that lifted cash and additional paid-in capital and roughly doubled stockholders' equity, and it repaid the amount drawn on its revolving line of credit, ending the second quarter with no debt outstanding. The trailing current ratio stands at 8.17, up from 3.79 at the end of 2025, reflecting the larger cash and marketable-securities balance against modest current liabilities. That net-cash position funds research, manufacturing capacity and working capital without recourse to new borrowing, which matters for a company that is not yet consistently profitable. Inventory and receivables are the working-capital lines to watch as revenue scales and as supply-chain delays move shipments between quarters.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation improved sharply in 2025. Operating cash flow was $21.3 million, reversing a $2.4 million use of cash in 2024, as the loss narrowed and working capital contributed. After capital expenditure, free cash flow was $12.3 million, a free-cash-flow margin of 4.7% and a trailing free-cash-flow yield of 1.8%. The company pays no dividend and did not repurchase stock, so internally generated cash and the recent equity raise both flow to the balance sheet rather than to shareholders. Free cash flow will likely stay uneven quarter to quarter, given the timing of defense-contract milestones and the supply-chain delays management has flagged.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: nLIGHT screens as expensive on every conventional profitability measure. The trailing P/E is negative at -164.8x because the company lost money over the last twelve months, so sales and forward earnings do more of the work. The shares trade at 7.6x trailing sales and about 83.1x next-twelve-month earnings, falling to roughly 65.4x on 2027 consensus EPS as profits are expected to scale. Those multiples embed much of the defense-driven growth the company is delivering. No peer-multiple comparison is available in the pack, where peer data is pending a source, so we anchor on nLIGHT's own trading history and on the Street's targets rather than on a comparable-company set. On that basis the valuation already prices in a lot: the Street's $88.86 consensus target, roughly double the current price, looks optimistic to us, and our range sits well below it.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Directed-energy and laser-sensing programs scale quickly, Aerospace and Defense demand stays strong, and the supply-chain delays clear. Revenue outpaces consensus, Products gross margin holds in the guided 34% to 40% band, and Adjusted EBITDA expands, driving a partial re-rating that recovers part of the drop from the 52-week high but stops short of the Street's more bullish targets.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Aerospace and Defense growth continues but moderates, and industrial and microfabrication demand grows more slowly. Revenue tracks the consensus path into 2027, margins improve gradually, and GAAP profitability arrives only late in the horizon. The multiple compresses from today's level as growth normalizes, leaving the shares modestly higher than the current price.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Supply-chain and China customs disruptions persist and pull revenue and margins below plan, defense program timing slips, and price erosion pressures gross margin. Losses widen again, the growth premium unwinds, and the shares fall about 27% from the current price toward the lower end of their 52-week range without necessarily reaching the $27.79 trough.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base case at 45%, the Bull at 30% and the Bear at 25%. Those weights blend to a fair value modestly above the current price, with positive but sub-one-to-one reward against the bear case. That combination derives a BUY, and we adopt it: the defense-driven inflection and net-cash balance sheet justify the constructive stance, while the rich multiple, GAAP losses and near-term supply-chain drag keep us from a stronger call.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The pack collapses nLIGHT to a single consolidated line, but the filing runs the business as two reportable segments. Laser Products, the merchant product business, contributed 71.9% of second-quarter 2026 revenue and grew 45.4% year over year, while Advanced Development, the funded research business, was the remaining 28.1% and grew 11.1%. By end market, Aerospace and Defense was 69.4% of the quarter, Industrial 14.6% and Microfabrication 16.0%, and all Advanced Development revenue sits inside the Aerospace and Defense market. Geographically, North America was 72.0% of second-quarter revenue, with EMEA and Asia Pacific the rest. The mix reconciles cleanly: the two segments and the three end markets each sum to 100% of the quarter, with no double-counting.

moatFactors.name: Vertical integration
moatFactors.body: nLIGHT designs and builds from the semiconductor chip through modules and system-level products, and reuses shared core technologies across defense, industrial and microfabrication applications. That vertical integration supports performance and supply control and is hard for a pure assembler to copy. It also loads the company with fixed U.S. manufacturing costs that weigh on margins when volumes dip.

moatFactors.name: Defense program entrenchment
moatFactors.body: Once a laser is designed into a defense platform, switching suppliers is slow and costly, which gives nLIGHT incumbency value on the programs it wins. Aerospace and Defense is the company's main end market and led the second quarter's growth. The flip side is dependence on government budgets, appropriations timing and prime-contractor decisions the company does not control.

moatFactors.name: Technology and IP
moatFactors.body: Sustained research spending in semiconductor and fiber lasers, directed energy and laser sensing underpins design wins, and the company reinvests a meaningful share of revenue in R&D each period. But the markets change quickly, average selling prices of mature products erode, and some competitors are larger and better resourced, so the technology edge must be continually re-earned.

moatFactors.name: Scale and cost position
moatFactors.body: nLIGHT is smaller than several competitors that have greater manufacturing, financial and R&D resources, and some rivals receive government subsidies or can integrate vertically by acquiring suppliers. That leaves nLIGHT a price-taker in parts of its markets and limits pricing power, especially in the industrial and microfabrication lines.

businessMoat.durability: The narrow moat should hold in defense but is thinner elsewhere. The defense franchise benefits from long program lifecycles, design-in switching costs and a secular push into directed energy, all of which are durable as long as budgets support the mission. The industrial and microfabrication lines face rapid technological change, price erosion and larger competitors, so their contribution to any moat is limited. The strong, net-cash balance sheet extends durability by funding research and capacity through cycles without new debt. On balance, we see a defensible but not wide position: enough to support attractive growth if defense demand persists, not enough on its own to guarantee pricing power or GAAP profitability.

points: Revenue growth has reaccelerated: after double-digit full-year 2025 growth, first-half 2026 revenue grew 43.5% to $162.8 million from $113.4 million a year earlier.
Defense is the engine of the reacceleration: 2025 Aerospace and Defense revenue grew 60% to $175.3 million on directed-energy programs, fiber-amplifier shipments and new awards.
Consensus expects the top line to keep compounding, to revenue of $305.9 million in 2026 and $347.1 million in 2027, up about 17% and then in the mid-teens.
Near-term growth is lumpy: third-quarter 2026 guidance of $63 million to $73 million implies a sequential step down, as shipments delayed by supply-chain and customs issues slip into later quarters.
Margin mix is improving as products scale: 2025 products gross margin reached 37.8%, up from 21.0% in 2024, which lifts incremental profitability as Laser Products volumes grow.

management.leadership: nLIGHT is led by Scott Keeney, its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, with Joseph Corso as Chief Financial Officer; the 2026 proxy names the two of them as the company's named executive officers for compensation purposes. Leadership has delivered a visible operational turn over the past year, with reaccelerating revenue, expanding gross margin and sharply narrower losses. Management is now handling two harder tasks at once, scaling defense production and navigating supply-chain and export-control disruption. Execution against near-term guidance, which was cut by delayed shipments, will be the test of credibility from here.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is growth-first and conservative on the liability side. nLIGHT pays no dividend and has not repurchased stock, reinvesting cash into research and manufacturing capacity instead. In early 2026 it raised equity, which lifted cash and roughly doubled stockholders' equity, and it repaid its drawn line of credit to end the second quarter with no debt. The trade-off is dilution: the equity raise and heavy stock-based compensation increase the share count, so per-share value depends on converting the defense opportunity into durable free cash flow rather than on financial leverage.
management.governance: Governance looks broadly sound for a company of this size, on the proxy excerpt in the pack. The board is majority independent: of the directors listed, only Scott Keeney and Camille Nichols are classified as not independent, Ms. Nichols because she served as Interim President of the company's nLIGHT DEFENSE Systems subsidiary from April 2024 through December 2024. Two directors, Bandel Carano and Raymond Link, are not standing for reelection, which will reduce the board to seven members after the annual meeting. The audit committee must approve related-party transactions, and the proxy reports no related-party transaction above $120,000 since the start of 2025. Pay is heavily performance-linked, with roughly 91% of the CEO's 2025 target compensation in equity and variable cash and only 9% in base salary, split evenly between time- and performance-based equity.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt in the pack covers board independence, compensation philosophy and related-party policy, but it does not include the beneficial-ownership table, so we make no specific claim on insider or institutional ownership stakes. What the excerpt does show is alignment through pay design, with the CEO's compensation weighted toward equity and long-term, performance-based awards tied to total shareholder return, including a special 2025 grant linked to stock-price thresholds.

idiosyncratic: Supply chain and trade policy are the clearest near-term risk. Components from certain non-U.S. suppliers, and some of nLIGHT's own shipments, have been held in customs in China, and China's June 2026 export-declaration rules have raised compliance costs and lengthened clearance times. Management has already pulled roughly $17 million of product revenue out of third-quarter guidance for this reason and warns of a material impact on revenue and profitability if the disruptions are not mitigated.

Customer and end-market concentration is high. Aerospace and Defense was 69.4% of second-quarter revenue, so results track government budgets, appropriations timing and prime-contractor decisions, and the company relies on a small number of customers for a large share of sales.

The company is not yet profitable on a GAAP basis and trades on rich multiples, so the valuation is sensitive to any growth or margin disappointment. Pricing power is limited by erosion in average selling prices on mature products and by larger, better-funded competitors, some of which receive government subsidies or can integrate vertically.

Execution risk rises with scale. Ramping defense production, sustaining yields and absorbing fixed U.S. manufacturing costs get harder as volumes grow, and margins can swing with product mix, contract cost estimates and capacity utilization.
risks.systemic: Systematically, nLIGHT is exposed to the defense-spending cycle, to global trade and tariff policy, and to the semiconductor and industrial capital-spending cycles. Defense budgets can shift with political priorities and appropriations delays; the 2026 tariff and export-control actions, including the Supreme Court's ruling on IEEPA tariffs and China's new export requirements, show how quickly cross-border rules can change. The microfabrication and industrial lines are tied to semiconductor-equipment and general economic cycles that have historically been volatile. As a smaller-capitalization company with high sensitivity to these forces, the shares are likely to stay more volatile than the broader market.

body: We rate nLIGHT a BUY. The case is a defense-led inflection in a company with a clean, net-cash balance sheet: revenue is reaccelerating, gross margin and Adjusted EBITDA have turned up, and directed energy gives a credible multi-year growth path. Our $46 to $68 target range brackets a probability-weighted fair value that sits well above the current price.

The rating is constructive, not aggressive. Reward versus risk is 0.79x, because the bear case still carries about a quarter of downside, the shares are richly valued on sales and forward earnings, and GAAP profitability has not arrived. We would treat the delayed third-quarter shipments and the pace of directed-energy awards as the things to watch: sustained delivery would support the higher end of our range, while a longer supply-chain disruption would validate the bear case.
